artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with its standard arc-length measure. For $1<p\le 2$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $f:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that
$$[f]_{W^{1/p,p}}^p:=\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy<\infty,$$
where $|x-y|$ is the arc-length distance on $S^1$. Every such map $f$ has a well-defined integer topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ (defined via approximation by smooth maps, since $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)\hookrightarrow \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$ for $p>1$).

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$, independent of $p$ and $f$, such that for every $1<p\le 2$ and every $f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$,
$$|\deg f|\;\le\; c\,(p-1)\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy\;?$$
artifact.category_tag: Fractional Sobolev maps and topological degree
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in Brezis's 2022/2024 collection of favorite open problems. Web searches did not surface a published resolution; related works (Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen estimates for the topological degree, Brezis–Mironescu's monograph on Sobolev maps to the circle) treat closely related estimates but do not appear to settle this specific uniform-in-$p$ inequality near $p=1$. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Selection of main open problems raised throughout his career, including degree estimates for fractional Sobolev maps into S^1.
status_evidence.claim: The degree estimate question for W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) near p=1 is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Sobolev Maps to the Circle (Brezis–Mironescu, 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatment of degree theory for Sobolev maps into S^1.
status_evidence.claim: Related degree estimates are studied but the uniform-in-p constant question is not resolved there.
